KEY MESSAGE 1...

A Tornado Watch is out for northeast Kentucky counties of Cater
and Greenup until 5am. This is due to robust helicity, abundant
shear and a the STP tornado parameter of 1+ which indicates 
possible tornadic environment not too mention tornadic activity
upstream.

Activity is already upstream and headed our way for the first 
push of convection into the area although the threat is 
weakening, therefore the watch is not being expanded anywhere. 
This watch may have to be expanded if trends persist west into 
our Ohio counties but the last tornado warning out west has 
expired therefore currently holding off on expanding at this 
time. 

Hi-res and convection allowing models (CAMs) have another push of 
convection in the form of a line settling in by mid morning. 
The HRRR, FV3 and NAM Nest are most aggressive and suggest 
potential super cellular activity with embedded thunderstorms 
along a line progressing southeast into our area moving south 
throughout the late morning and into the afternoon. 

With enough instability for the late morning and afternoon 
storms will be able to continue under a strong low level jet 
support and high shear to promote a damaging wind threat as well
as tornadic threat with rotating showers possible along the 
line or from super cellular storms. Even though prior 
convection will weaken instability the line will have enough 
support to keep going through the area, however it may not be as
potent as other models suggest. 

The winds will be a thing to watch as shower and thunderstorm 
activity will have a good environment with high DCAPE and high 
PWATs to promote downbursts and heavy downpours which could 
promote flooding potential, however it should be more isolated 
in nature and be more apparent across low lying or flood prone 
areas unless training occurs elsewhere. One caveat is that the 
line will be moving fast with strong steering flow aloft which 
may deter flash flooding all together this late morning and
afternoon.

Unless rates exceed flash flood guidance or rather 
2+ inches per hour or high rates affect an area repeatedly or 
under training will possibly cause issues to the aforementioned 
areas and elsewhere. Shower activity could bring down strong 
winds which could be damaging and severe but this will involve 
convection rather than synoptic winds which made the decision of
holding off on a wind advisory being issued at this time.

By mid morning, the tornado threat diminishes and only a 
damaging wind threat will remain, however we cannot rule out a 
quick spin up along the line as the cold front sags south into 
the southern portions of our county warning area. Due to our 
radar being down it will be hard to detect low level rotation 
therefore shower activity or heavy thunderstorm activity will 
likely be warned on if there is any indication of rotation or a 
meso even though the tornadic environment will be diminishing. 

As the line exits toward the south another push of convection is 
indicated by some of the Hi-res models coming in from the west 
to affect our southern half of the area. This will add to QPF 
values but the activity will be across our driest portions of 
our CWA, so basically no flood watch is needed and will be
handled by the warning process.

WPC does have us in a slight risk for a excessive rainfall 
threat for this area so isolated flooding issues could occur in 
areas susceptible to flood or drainage issues. This activity 
will be coming in behind the front, therefore much of the 
instability will be used up so the environment should not pose 
a severe threat. 

After the aforementioned convection subsides things will clear 
out and any activity will exit by early afternoon opening the 
area up to a dry rest of the day on Friday and into the weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

High pressure at the surface and a semi flat ridge aloft will 
help keep the weekend settled although by late Sunday a low 
pressure system will traverse into the region just north of us 
and drop down a weak frontal band for Monday. Models have this
feature weakening as it comes through the area so frontolysis is
likely. 

Thereafter, zonal flow will settle in and keep the area safe 
until Thursday as a short wave moves into the region which could
promote chances for diurnal convection on next Thursday 
afternoon and evening.
